units.zh: 楊愔 燕子獻 宋欽道 鄭頤
units.en: Yang Yin; Yan Zixian; Song Qindao; Zheng Yi
units.literal: Yang Yin; Yan Zixian; Song Qindao; Zheng Yi

units.zh: 楊愔，字遵彥，小名秦王，弘農華陰人。
units.en: Yang Yin, styled Zunyin, childhood name Prince of Qin, was from Huayin in Hongnong.
units.literal: Yang Yin, styled Zunyin, childhood name Prince of Qin, was a man of Huayin in Hongnong.

units.zh: 父津，魏時累為司空侍中。
units.en: His father Jin had served Wei repeatedly as director of works and palace attendant.
units.literal: His father Jin in Wei times rose repeatedly to Director of Works and Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 愔兒童時，口若不能言，而風度深敏，出入門閭，未嘗戲弄。
units.en: As a child Yin seemed barely able to speak, yet was deeply perceptive in manner; in and out of the household gates he never played about.
units.literal: In childhood Yin seemed as though he could not speak, yet was deep and keen in manner; going in and out of gates, he never played about.

units.zh: 六歲學史書，十一受《詩》、《易》，好《左氏春秋》。
units.en: At six he studied historical works; at eleven he took up the Odes and the Changes, and loved the Zuo Tradition of the Spring and Autumn Annals.
units.literal: At six he studied historical works; at eleven he received the Odes and the Changes, and loved the Zuo Tradition of the Spring and Autumn Annals.

units.zh: 幼喪母，曾詣舅源子恭，子恭與之飲，問讀何書，曰：「誦《詩》。」
units.en: He lost his mother young and once visited his maternal uncle Yuan Zigong; Zigong drank with him and asked what book he was reading. He said, "I am reciting the Odes."
units.literal: He lost his mother young and once went to his maternal uncle Yuan Zigong; Zigong drank with him and asked what book he was reading. He said: "I am reciting the Odes."

units.zh: 子恭曰：「誦至《渭陽》未邪？」
units.en: Zigong said, "Have you recited as far as 'On the Wei-yang'?"
units.literal: Zigong said: "Have you recited as far as 'On the Wei-yang'?"

units.zh: 愔便號泣感噎，子恭亦對之歔欷，遂為之罷酒。
units.en: Yin at once wailed and choked with grief; Zigong wept in answer, and thereupon stopped the drinking.
units.literal: Yin at once wailed and choked with grief; Zigong wept in answer, and thereupon stopped the drinking.

units.zh: 子恭後謂津曰：「常謂秦王不甚察慧，從今已後，更欲刮目視之。」
units.en: Later Zigong said to Jin, "I always said Prince of Qin was not very sharp; from now on I shall view him with new eyes."
units.literal: Later Zigong said to Jin: "I always said Prince of Qin was not very sharp; from now on I shall view him with new eyes."

units.zh: 愔一門四世同居，家甚隆盛，昆季就學者三十餘人。
units.en: One household in Yin's clan lived together four generations; the family was very prosperous, and more than thirty brothers and cousins went to school.
units.literal: One household in Yin's clan lived together four generations; the family was very prosperous, and more than thirty brothers and cousins went to school.

units.zh: 學庭前有柰樹，實落地，群兒咸爭之，愔頹然獨坐。
units.en: Before the school court stood a crabapple tree; when fruit fell to the ground the boys all scrambled for it, while Yin sat apart in calm.
units.literal: Before the school court stood a crabapple tree; when fruit fell to the ground the boys all scrambled for it, while Yin sat apart in calm.

units.zh: 其季父暐適入學館，見之大用嗟異，顧謂賓客曰：「此兒恬裕，有我家風。」
units.en: His uncle Wei happened to enter the school hall, saw it, and greatly marveled; turning to the guests he said, "This boy is tranquil and ample—he has our family's air."
units.literal: His uncle Wei happened to enter the school hall, saw it, and greatly marveled; turning to the guests he said: "This boy is tranquil and ample—he has our family's air."

units.zh: 宅內有茂竹，遂為愔於林邊別葺一室，命獨處其中，常以銅盤具盛饌以飯之。
units.en: Within the residence were thick bamboos; he therefore built a separate room for Yin at the edge of the grove and ordered him to live there alone, regularly serving him a full meal in a bronze tray.
units.literal: Within the residence were thick bamboos; he therefore built a separate room for Yin at the edge of the grove and ordered him to live there alone, regularly serving him a full meal in a bronze tray.

units.zh: 因以督厲諸子曰：「汝輩但如遵彥謹慎，自得竹林別室、銅盤重肉之食。」
units.en: He thereby urged and admonished the sons, saying, "You need only be as careful as Zunyin, and you will yourselves win a bamboo-grove chamber and bronze-tray feasts of heavy meat."
units.literal: He thereby urged and admonished the sons, saying: "You need only be as careful as Zunyin, and you will yourselves win a bamboo grove chamber and bronze-tray feasts of heavy meat."

units.zh: 愔從父兄黃門侍郎昱特相器重，曾謂人曰：「此兒駒齒未落，已是我家龍文。
units.en: Yin's cousin by the father's line, palace attendant Yu, especially valued him and once told others, "This boy's colt teeth have not yet fallen, yet already he is our family's dragon pattern.
units.literal: Yin's cousin by the father's line, Palace Attendant Yu, especially valued him and once told others: "This boy's colt teeth have not yet fallen, yet already he is our family's dragon pattern.

units.zh: 更十歲後，當求之千里外。」
units.en: Ten years hence you will have to seek him a thousand li away."
units.literal: Ten years hence you will have to seek him a thousand li away."

units.zh: 昱嘗與十餘人賦詩，愔一覽便誦，無所遺失。
units.en: Yu once composed a poem with more than ten men; Yin read it once and recited it, missing nothing.
units.literal: Yu once composed a poem with more than ten men; Yin read it once and recited it, missing nothing.

units.zh: 及長，能清言，美音制，風神俊悟，容止可觀。
units.en: When grown he could hold pure talk, had a fine voice, was spiritually handsome and quick of wit, and his bearing was worth watching.
units.literal: When grown he could discourse in pure talk, had a fine voice, was spiritually handsome and quick of wit, and his bearing was worth watching.

units.zh: 人士見之，莫不敬異，有識者多以遠大許之。
units.en: Gentlemen who met him all regarded him with respect and wonder; those with insight mostly promised him a far-reaching future.
units.literal: Gentlemen who met him all regarded him with respect and wonder; those with insight mostly promised him a far-reaching future.

units.zh: 正光中，隨父之幷州。
units.en: In the Zhenguang era he followed his father to Bing province.
units.literal: In the Zhenguang era he followed his father to Bing province.

units.zh: 性旣恬默，又好山水，遂入晉陽西縣甕山讀書。
units.en: His nature being tranquil and silent and also fond of mountains and rivers, he entered Weng Mountain in Jinyang West county to read books.
units.literal: His nature being tranquil and silent and also fond of mountains and rivers, he entered Weng Mountain in Jinyang West county to read books.

units.zh: 孝昌初，津為定州刺史，愔亦隨父之職。
units.en: At the beginning of Xiaochang, Jin became inspector of Dingzhou and Yin also followed his father to his post.
units.literal: At the beginning of Xiaochang, Jin became inspector of Dingzhou and Yin also followed his father to his post.

units.zh: 以軍功除羽林監，賜爵魏昌男，不拜。
units.en: For military merit he was made supervisor of the Feathered Forest, enfeoffed as Baron of Weichang, and did not accept.
units.literal: For military merit he was made supervisor of the Feathered Forest, enfeoffed as Marquis of Weichang, and did not accept.

units.zh: 及中山為杜洛周陷，全家被囚縶。
units.en: When Zhongshan fell to Du Luozhou, the whole family was taken prisoner.
units.literal: When Zhongshan fell to Du Luozhou, the whole family was taken prisoner.

units.zh: 未幾，洛周滅，又沒葛榮。
units.en: Before long Luozhou was destroyed and they fell again to Ge Rong.
units.literal: Before long Luozhou was destroyed and they fell again to Ge Rong.

units.zh: 榮欲以女妻之，又逼以偽職。
units.en: Rong wished to marry his daughter to him and also pressed a false office on him.
units.literal: Rong wished to marry his daughter to him and also pressed a false office on him.

units.zh: 愔乃託疾，密含牛血數合，於衆中吐之，仍佯喑不語。
units.en: Yin then feigned illness, secretly held several he of ox blood in his mouth, spat it out in the crowd, and still pretended to be mute and speechless.
units.literal: Yin then feigned illness, secretly held several he of ox blood in his mouth, spat it out in the crowd, and still pretended to be mute and speechless.

units.zh: 榮以為信然，乃止。
units.en: Rong believed it real and thereupon stopped.
units.literal: Rong believed it real and thereupon stopped.

units.zh: 永安初，還洛，拜通直散騎侍郎，時年十八。
units.en: At the beginning of Yong'an he returned to Luoyang and was appointed attendant gentleman of the unimpeded staff; he was then eighteen.
units.literal: At the beginning of Yong'an he returned to Luoyang and was appointed attendant gentleman of the Unimpeded Staff; he was then eighteen.

units.zh: 元顥入洛，時愔從父兄侃為北中郎將，鎮河梁。
units.en: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Yin at the time had a cousin Kan serving as general of the north center, garrisoning He Bridge.
units.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Yin at the time had a cousin Kan serving as General of the North Center, garrisoning He Bridge.

units.zh: 愔適至侃處，便屬乘輿失守，夜至河。
units.en: Yin happened to reach Kan's post just as the imperial carriage lost its place; at night they came to the river.
units.literal: Yin happened to reach Kan's post just as the imperial carriage lost its place; at night they came to the river.

units.zh: 侃雖奉迎車駕北渡，而潛欲南奔，愔固諫止之。
units.en: Though Kan received the carriage and escorted it north across the river, in secret he wished to flee south; Yin firmly remonstrated and stopped him.
units.literal: Though Kan received the carriage and escorted it north across the river, in secret he wished to flee south; Yin firmly remonstrated and stopped him.

units.zh: 遂相與扈從達建州。
units.en: They thereupon together escorted the court as far as Jian province.
units.literal: They thereupon together escorted the court as far as Jian province.

units.zh: 除通直散騎常侍。
units.en: He was made regular attendant gentleman of the unimpeded staff.
units.literal: He was made regular attendant gentleman of the Unimpeded Staff.

units.zh: 愔以世故未夷，志在潛退，乃謝病，與友人中直侍郎河間邢卲隱於嵩山。
units.en: Yin, because worldly troubles were not yet settled, wished to withdraw in seclusion; he therefore pleaded illness and with his friend Hejian Xing Shao, attendant gentleman of the central straight, hid on Mount Song.
units.literal: Yin, because worldly troubles were not yet settled, wished to withdraw in seclusion; he therefore pleaded illness and with his friend Hejian Xing Shao, attendant gentleman of the Central Straight, hid on Mount Song.

units.zh: 及莊帝誅尒朱榮，其從兄侃參贊帷幄。
units.en: When Emperor Zhuang executed Erzhu Rong, his cousin Kan took part in planning within the curtains.
units.literal: When Emperor Zhuang executed Erzhu Rong, his cousin Kan took part in planning within the curtains.

units.zh: 朝廷以其父津為幷州刺史、北道大行臺，愔隨之任。
units.en: The court made his father Jin inspector of Bingzhou and grand commissioner of the northern route; Yin followed him to his appointment.
units.literal: The court made his father Jin inspector of Bingzhou and grand commissioner of the northern route; Yin followed him to his appointment.

units.zh: 有邯鄲人楊寬者，求義從出藩，愔請津納之。
units.en: There was a Handan man named Yang Kuan who sought to follow in righteous service when Jin went out to his province; Yin asked Jin to take him in.
units.literal: There was a Handan man named Yang Kuan who sought to follow in righteous service when Jin went out to his province; Yin asked Jin to take him in.

units.zh: 俄而孝莊幽崩，愔時適欲還都，行達邯鄲，過楊寬家，為寬所執。
units.en: Before long Emperor Xiaozhuang was imprisoned and died; Yin at the time was about to return to the capital, reached Handan on the road, passed Yang Kuan's house, and was seized by Kuan.
units.literal: Before long Emperor Xiaozhuang was imprisoned and died; Yin at the time was about to return to the capital, reached Handan on the road, passed Yang Kuan's house, and was seized by Kuan.

units.zh: 至相州，見刺史劉誕，以愔名家盛德，甚相哀念，付長史慕容白澤禁止焉。
units.en: Reaching Xiang province he saw inspector Liu Yan; because Yin was of a famous house and lofty virtue, Yan greatly pitied him and handed him to chief clerk Murong Baize to detain.
units.literal: Reaching Xiang province he saw Inspector Liu Yan; because Yin was of a famous house and lofty virtue, Yan greatly pitied him and handed him to Chief Clerk Murong Baize to detain.

units.zh: 遣隊主鞏榮貴防禁送都。
units.en: He sent squad chief Gong Ronggui to guard and escort him to the capital.
units.literal: He sent squad chief Gong Ronggui to guard and escort him to the capital.

units.zh: 至安陽亭，愔謂榮貴曰：「僕家世忠臣，輸誠魏室，家亡國破，一至於此。
units.en: At Anyang Pavilion Yin said to Ronggui, "My house for generations has been loyal ministers, pouring sincerity into the Wei house; now family is destroyed and state broken—things have come to this.
units.literal: At Anyang Pavilion Yin said to Ronggui: "My house for generations has been loyal ministers, pouring sincerity into the Wei house; now family is destroyed and state broken—things have come to this.

units.zh: 雖曰囚虜，復何面目見君父之讐仇！
units.en: Though called a captive, what face have I to see our lord and father's mortal foes!
units.literal: Though called a captive, what face have I to see our lord and father's mortal foes!

units.zh: 得自縊於一繩，傳首而去，君之惠也。」
units.en: If I may hang myself on one cord and send my head away, that will be your kindness."
units.literal: If I may hang myself on one cord and send my head away, that will be your kindness."

units.zh: 榮貴深相憐感，遂與俱逃。
units.en: Ronggui deeply pitied and was moved, and thereupon fled together with him.
units.literal: Ronggui deeply pitied and was moved, and thereupon fled with him together.

units.zh: 愔乃投高昂兄弟。
units.en: Yin then threw himself on Gao Ao's brothers.
units.literal: Yin then threw himself on Gao Ao's brothers.

units.zh: 旣潛竄累載，屬神武至信都，遂投刺轅門。
units.en: Having lurked in hiding for several years, when Gao Huan reached Xindu he thereupon presented his card at the camp gate.
units.literal: Having lurked in hiding for several years, when Gao Huan reached Xindu he thereupon presented his card at the camp gate.

units.zh: 便蒙引見，贊揚興運，陳訴家禍，言辭哀壯，涕泗橫集，神武為之改容。
units.en: He was at once granted audience, praised the rising fortune, and stated his family's calamity; his words were mournful and strong, tears streamed across his face, and Gao Huan changed countenance for it.
units.literal: He was at once granted audience, praised the rising fortune, and stated his family's calamity; his words were mournful and strong, tears streamed across his face, and Gao Huan changed countenance for it.

units.zh: 即署行臺郎中。
units.en: He was immediately appointed gentleman of the mobile staff.
units.literal: He was immediately appointed gentleman of the mobile staff.

units.zh: 大軍南攻鄴，歷楊寬村，寬於馬前叩頭請罪。
units.en: When the great army attacked Ye southward and passed Yang Kuan's village, Kuan knelt before the horse and begged forgiveness.
units.literal: When the great army attacked Ye southward and passed Yang Kuan's village, Kuan knelt before the horse and begged forgiveness.

units.zh: 愔謂曰：「人不識恩義，蓋亦常理，我不恨卿，無遐驚怖。」
units.en: Yin said to him, "Men not knowing grace and righteousness is also the ordinary rule; I bear you no hatred—have no distant terror."
units.literal: Yin said to him: "Men not knowing grace and righteousness is also the ordinary rule; I bear you no hatred—have no distant terror."

units.zh: 時鄴未下，神武命愔作祭天文，燎畢而城陷。
units.en: At the time Ye had not yet fallen; Gao Huan ordered Yin to compose the text for a sacrifice to Heaven; when the burning was done the city fell.
units.literal: At the time Ye had not yet fallen; Gao Huan ordered Yin to compose the text for a sacrifice to Heaven; when the burning was done the city fell.

units.zh: 由是轉大行臺右丞。
units.en: Thereupon he was transferred to right aide of the grand mobile staff.
units.literal: Thereupon he was transferred to right aide of the grand mobile staff.

units.zh: 于時霸圖草創，軍國務廣，文檄教令，皆自愔及崔㥄悛出。
units.en: At that time the hegemonic design was newly begun and military and state affairs were broad; proclamations, orders, and edicts all issued from Yin and Cui Lingquan.
units.literal: At that time the hegemonic design was newly begun and military and state affairs were broad; proclamations, orders, and edicts all issued from Yin and Cui Ling-Quan.

units.zh: 遭離家難，以喪禮自居，所食唯鹽米而已，哀毀骨立。
units.en: Having met family disaster, he took mourning ritual as his own rule; what he ate was only salt and rice, and in grief he wasted until only bone remained.
units.literal: Having met family disaster, he took mourning ritual as his own rule; what he ate was only salt and rice, and in grief he wasted until only bone remained.

units.zh: 神武愍之，恒相開慰。
units.en: Gao Huan pitied him and constantly comforted him.
units.literal: Gao Huan pitied him and constantly comforted him.

units.zh: 及韓陵之戰，愔每陣先登，朋僚咸共怪嘆曰：「楊氏儒生，今遂為武士，仁者必勇，定非虛論。」
units.en: At the battle of Hanling, Yin each time took the van in the line; colleagues all marveled together and said, "The Yang clan's Confucian—now he has become a warrior; the benevolent must be brave—surely no empty saying."
units.literal: At the battle of Hanling, Yin each time took the van in the line; colleagues all marveled together and said: "The Yang clan's Confucian—now he has become a warrior; the benevolent must be brave—surely no empty saying."

units.zh: 頃之，表請解職還葬。
units.en: Before long he memorialized asking to leave office and return for burial.
units.literal: Before long he memorialized asking to leave office and return for burial.

units.zh: 一門之內，贈太師、太傅、丞相、大將軍者二人，太尉、錄尚書及中書令者三人，僕射、尚書者五人，刺史、太守者二十餘人。
units.en: Within one gate, two men had been posthumously given grand preceptor, grand tutor, chancellor, and grand general; three had been grand commandant, recorder of the masters of writing, and director of the secretariat; five had been vice directors and masters of writing; more than twenty had been inspectors and grand administrators.
units.literal: Within one gate, two men had been posthumously given Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, chancellor, and grand general; three had been Grand Commandant, recorder of the masters of writing, and director of the secretariat; five had been vice directors and masters of writing; more than twenty had been inspectors and grand administrators.

units.zh: 追榮之盛，古今未之有也。
units.en: The glory of posthumous honors—never had there been such in past and present.
units.literal: The glory of posthumous honors—never had there been such in past and present.

units.zh: 及喪柩進發，吉凶儀衛亙二十餘里，會葬者將萬人。
units.en: When the coffin set out, auspicious and inauspicious guards and escorts stretched more than twenty li; those attending the burial were nearly ten thousand.
units.literal: When the coffin set out, auspicious and inauspicious guards and escorts stretched more than twenty li; those attending the burial were nearly ten thousand.

units.zh: 是日隆冬盛寒，風雪嚴厚，愔跣步號哭，見者無不哀之。
units.en: That day was deep winter and bitter cold, wind and snow severe and thick; Yin walked barefoot wailing, and those who saw it were without exception moved to pity.
units.literal: That day was deep winter and bitter cold, wind and snow severe and thick; Yin walked barefoot wailing, and those who saw it were without exception moved to pity.

units.zh: 尋徵赴晉陽，仍居本職。
units.en: Before long he was summoned to Jinyang and still held his former post.
units.literal: Before long he was summoned to Jinyang and still held his former post.

units.zh: 愔從兄幼卿為岐州刺史，以直言忤旨見誅。
units.en: Yin's cousin Youqing was inspector of Qi province; for blunt words that offended the intent he was put to death.
units.literal: Yin's cousin Youqing was inspector of Qi province; for blunt words that offended the intent he was put to death.

units.zh: 愔聞之悲懼，因哀感發疾，後取急就雁門溫湯療疾。
units.en: When Yin heard it he was grieved and afraid; grief and shock brought on illness, and later he took urgent leave to go to the hot springs at Yanmen to treat his illness.
units.literal: When Yin heard it he was grieved and afraid; grief and shock brought on illness, and later he took urgent leave to go to the hot springs at Yanmen to treat his illness.

units.zh: 郭秀素害其能，因致書恐之曰：「高王欲送卿於帝所。」
units.en: Guo Xiu by nature envied his ability and therefore sent a letter threatening him, saying, "The Prince of Qi wishes to send you to the Emperor's place."
units.literal: Guo Xiu by nature envied his ability and therefore sent a letter threatening him, saying: "The Prince of Qi wishes to send you to the Emperor's place."

units.zh: 仍勸其逃亡。
units.en: He also urged him to flee.
units.literal: He also urged him to flee.

units.zh: 愔遂棄衣冠於水濱若自沉者，變易名姓，自稱劉士安，入嵩山，與沙門曇謨徵等居成削迹。
units.en: Yin thereupon cast off hat and robes at the water's edge as though drowning himself, changed his name, called himself Liu Shi'an, entered Mount Song, and with the monk Tan Mo and others dwelt in seclusion, his traces cut away.
units.literal: Yin thereupon cast off hat and robes at the water's edge as though drowning himself, changed his name, called himself Liu Shi'an, entered Mount Song, and with the monk Tan Mo and others dwelt in seclusion, his traces cut away.

units.zh: 又潛之光州，因東入田橫島，以講誦為業。
units.en: He also lurked in Guang province and then went east into Tianheng Island, making lecturing and recitation his livelihood.
units.literal: He also lurked in Guang province and then went east into Tianheng Island, making lecturing and recitation his livelihood.

units.zh: 海隅之士，謂之劉先生。
units.en: Gentlemen of the sea's edge called him Master Liu.
units.literal: Gentlemen of the sea's edge called him Master Liu.

units.zh: 太守王元景陰佑之。
units.en: Grand administrator Wang Yuanjing secretly aided him.
units.literal: Grand Administrator Wang Yuanjing secretly aided him.

units.zh: 神武知愔存，遣愔從兄寶猗賫書慰喻，仍遣光州刺史奚思業令搜訪，以禮發遣。
units.en: Gao Huan knew Yin was alive, sent Yin's cousin Baoyi with a letter to comfort and instruct him, and still sent Guangzhou inspector Xi Siye to search him out and send him off with ritual.
units.literal: Gao Huan knew Yin was alive, sent Yin's cousin Baoyi with a letter to comfort and instruct him, and still sent Guangzhou inspector Xi Siye to search him out and send him off with ritual.

units.zh: 神武見之悅，除太原公開府司馬，轉長史，復授大行臺右丞，封華陰縣侯，遷給事黃門侍郎，妻以庶女。
units.en: Gao Huan was pleased to see him, made him staff officer of the Prince of Taiyuan's establishment, transferred him to chief clerk, again gave him right aide of the grand mobile staff, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Huayin county, promoted him to attendant gentleman of the yellow gate, and gave him a concubine's daughter in marriage.
units.literal: Gao Huan was pleased to see him, made him staff officer of the Prince of Taiyuan's establishment, transferred him to chief clerk, again gave him right aide of the grand mobile staff, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Huayin county, promoted him to attendant gentleman of the Yellow Gate, and gave him a concubine's daughter in marriage.

units.zh: 又兼散騎常侍，為聘梁使主。
units.en: He also concurrently served as regular attendant gentleman and was chief envoy on a mission of betrothal to Liang.
units.literal: He also concurrently served as regular attendant gentleman and was chief envoy on a mission of betrothal to Liang.

units.zh: 至碻磝戍，州內有愔家舊佛寺，入精廬禮拜，見太傅容像，悲感慟哭，嘔血數升，遂發病不成行，輿疾還鄴。
units.en: Reaching Qiaoqiu garrison, within the prefecture was an old Buddhist temple of Yin's family; he entered the pure hall to bow in worship, saw the image of the grand tutor, was moved to grief and wailed, vomited several sheng of blood, and thereupon fell ill and could not travel; he was carried ill back to Ye.
units.literal: Reaching Qiaoqiu garrison, within the prefecture was an old Buddhist temple of Yin's family; he entered the pure hall to bow in worship, saw the image of the Grand Tutor, was moved to grief and wailed, vomited several sheng of blood, and thereupon fell ill and could not travel; he was carried ill back to Ye.

units.zh: 久之，以本官兼尚書吏部郎中。
units.en: After a long while, in his former office he was made concurrently gentleman of the ministry of personnel in the masters of writing.
units.literal: After a long while, in his former office he was made concurrently gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel in the masters of writing.

units.zh: 武定末，以望實之美，超拜吏部尚書，加侍中、衛將軍，侍學典選如故。
units.en: At the end of Wuding, for the beauty of his reputation and substance he was promoted over others to director of the ministry of personnel, with concurrent palace attendant and guards general; he attended study and directed selection as before.
units.literal: At the end of Wuding, for the beauty of his reputation and substance he was promoted over others to director of the ministry of personnel, with concurrent palace attendant and guards general; he attended study and directed selection as before.

units.zh: 天保初，以本官領太子少傅，別封陽夏縣男。
units.en: At the beginning of Tianbao, in his former office he was made heir apparent junior tutor and separately enfeoffed as Baron of Yangxia county.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, in his former office he was made heir apparent junior tutor and separately enfeoffed as Baron of Yangxia county.

units.zh: 又詔監太史，遷尚書右僕射。
units.en: An edict also ordered him to supervise the grand astrologer; he was moved to right vice director of the masters of writing.
units.literal: An edict also ordered him to supervise the Grand Astrologer; he was moved to right vice director of the masters of writing.

units.zh: 尚太原長公主，即魏孝靜後也。
units.en: He married the Princess of Taiyuan, who was Empress Xiaojing of Wei.
units.literal: He married the Princess of Taiyuan, who was Empress Xiaojing of Wei.

units.zh: 會有雉集其舍，又拜開府儀同三司、尚書左僕射，改封華山郡公。
units.en: Once a pheasant alighted on his residence; he was again appointed commissioner with the same ceremonial as the three excellencies and left vice director of the masters of writing, and his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Huashan commandery.
units.literal: Once a pheasant alighted on his residence; he was again appointed commissioner with the same ceremonial as the Three Excellencies and left vice director of the masters of writing, and his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Huashan commandery.

units.zh: 九年，徙尚書令，又拜特進、驃騎大將軍。
units.en: In the ninth year he was moved to director of the masters of writing and again appointed special emissary and general of agile cavalry.
units.literal: In the ninth year he was moved to director of the masters of writing and again appointed special emissary and general of agile cavalry.

units.zh: 十年，封開封王。
units.en: In the tenth year he was enfeoffed as Prince of Kaifeng.
units.literal: In the tenth year he was enfeoffed as Prince of Kaifeng.

units.zh: 文宣之崩，百僚莫有下淚，愔悲不自勝。
units.en: When Gao Yang died, among the hundred officials none shed tears; Yin grieved beyond bearing.
units.literal: When Gao Yang died, among the hundred officials none shed tears; Yin grieved beyond bearing.

units.zh: 濟南嗣業，任遇益隆，朝章國命，一人而已，推誠體道，時無異議。
units.en: Jinan succeeded to the enterprise; his appointment and favor grew still greater; court regulations and state commands were his alone—he extended sincerity and embodied the Way, and for a time there was no dissenting voice.
units.literal: Jinan succeeded to the enterprise; his appointment and favor grew still greater; court regulations and state commands were his alone—he extended sincerity and embodied the Way, and for a time there was no dissenting voice.

units.zh: 乾明元年二月，為孝昭帝所誅，時年五十。
units.en: In the second month of the first year of Qianming he was executed by Emperor Xiaozhao; he was then fifty.
units.literal: In the second month of the first year of Qianming he was executed by Emperor Xiaozhao; he was then fifty.

units.zh: 天統末，追贈司空。
units.en: At the end of Tiantong he was posthumously given director of works.
units.literal: At the end of Tiantong he was posthumously given Director of Works.

units.zh: 愔貴公子，早著聲譽，風表鑒裁，為朝野所稱。
units.en: Yin was a nobleman's son who early won reputation; his bearing, judgment, and discernment were praised by court and countryside alike.
units.literal: Yin was a nobleman's son who early won reputation; his bearing, judgment, and discernment were praised by court and countryside alike.

units.zh: 家門遇禍，唯有二弟一妹及兄孫女數人，撫養孤幼，慈旨溫顏，咸出人表。
units.en: When his house met calamity, only two younger brothers, one younger sister, and several elder brother's granddaughters remained; he reared the orphaned young with kind intent and warm countenance, all beyond the common measure.
units.literal: When his house met calamity, only two younger brothers, one younger sister, and several elder brother's granddaughters remained; he reared the orphaned young with kind intent and warm countenance, all beyond the common measure.

units.zh: 重義輕財，前後賜與，多散之親族，羣從弟侄十數人，並待而舉火。
units.en: He valued righteousness and held wealth light; gifts before and after he mostly scattered among kin; more than ten younger cousins and nephews all depended on him for their cooking fires.
units.literal: He valued righteousness and held wealth light; gifts before and after he mostly scattered among kin; more than ten younger cousins and nephews all depended on him for their cooking fires.

units.zh: 頻遭迍厄，冒履艱危，一飧之惠，酬答必重，性命之讐，捨而不問。
units.en: Repeatedly meeting adversity, he braved hardship and danger; a single meal's kindness he repaid heavily; a life-and-death foe he could set aside and not inquire after.
units.literal: Repeatedly meeting adversity, he braved hardship and danger; a single meal's kindness he repaid heavily; a life-and-death foe he could set aside and not inquire after.

units.zh: 典選二十餘年，獎擢人倫，以為己任，然取士多以言貌，時致謗言，以為愔之用人，似貧士市瓜，取其大者。
units.en: Directing selection for more than twenty years, he promoted human worth and took it as his own charge; yet in taking gentlemen he mostly relied on words and looks, and at times drew slander—people said Yin's employing of men was like a poor man buying melons, taking the big ones.
units.literal: Directing selection for more than twenty years, he promoted human worth and took it as his own charge; yet in taking gentlemen he mostly relied on words and looks, and at times drew slander—people said Yin's employing of men was like a poor man buying melons, taking the big ones.

units.zh: 愔聞，不屑焉。
units.en: When Yin heard it he disdained to heed it.
units.literal: When Yin heard it he disdained to heed it.

units.zh: 其聰記強識，半面不忘。
units.en: His clever memory and strong retention—half a face once seen, never forgotten.
units.literal: His clever memory and strong retention—half a face once seen, never forgotten.

units.zh: 每有所召問，或單稱姓，或單稱名，無有誤者。
units.en: Whenever he was summoned and questioned, whether only the surname or only the given name was spoken, there was never a mistake.
units.literal: Whenever he was summoned and questioned, whether only the surname or only the given name was spoken, there was never a mistake.

units.zh: 後有選人魯漫漢，自言猥賤，獨不見識。
units.en: Later there was a candidate Lu Manhan who said of himself that he was base and lowly and alone went unrecognized.
units.literal: Later there was a candidate Lu Manhan who said of himself that he was base and lowly and alone went unrecognized.

units.zh: 愔曰：「卿前在元子思坊，騎禿尾草驢，經見我不下，以方麴曲鄣面，我何不識卿？」
units.en: Yin said, "You before, in Yuan Zisi's lane, rode a bald-tailed grass donkey; passing me you did not dismount; you screened your face with square-curled bread—how should I not know you?"
units.literal: Yin said: "You before, in Yuan Zisi's lane, rode a bald-tailed grass donkey; passing me you did not dismount; you screened your face with square-curled bread—how should I not know you?"

units.zh: 漫漢驚服。
units.en: Manhan was startled and submitted.
units.literal: Manhan was startled and submitted.

units.zh: 又調之曰：「名以定體，漫漢果自不虛。」
units.en: He also teased him, saying, "The name fixes the substance—Manhan indeed is not empty."
units.literal: He also teased him, saying: "The name fixes the substance—Manhan indeed is not empty."

units.zh: 又令吏唱人名，誤以盧士深為士琛，士琛自言，愔曰：「盧郎玉潤，所以從玉。」
units.en: He also had a clerk call out men's names and by mistake took Lu Shishen for Shichen; Shichen spoke up himself, and Yin said, "Master Lu is jade-lustrous—therefore the jade radical."
units.literal: He also had a clerk call out men's names and by mistake called Lu Shishen Shichen; Shichen spoke up himself, and Yin said: "Master Lu, jade lustrous—therefore the jade radical. From nature it is so."

units.zh: 自尚公主後，衣紫羅袍，金縷大帶。
units.en: After he married the princess he wore purple gauze robes and a great belt threaded with gold.
units.literal: After marrying the princess he wore purple gauze robes and a great belt with gold thread.

units.zh: 遇李庶，頗以為恥，謂曰：「我此衣服，都是內裁，旣見子將，不能無愧。」
units.en: When he met Li Shu he was ashamed and said, "These clothes were all cut in the inner palace; now that I have seen you, my general, I cannot help feeling shame."
units.literal: Meeting Li Shu, he was quite ashamed and said, "These clothes of mine were all cut within the palace; now that I have seen you, my general, I cannot be without shame."

units.zh: 及居端揆，權綜機衡，千端萬緒，神無滯用。
units.en: Once he stood at the head of government and held the levers of power, ten thousand matters came before him and his mind never lagged.
units.literal: When he occupied the summit of government, power embraced the pivots of state; ten thousand ends and threads—his spirit had no sluggish application.

units.zh: 自天保五年已後，一人喪德，維持匡救，實有賴焉。
units.en: From the fifth year of Tianbao onward, when the emperor lost his virtue, the realm's stability and repair truly depended on him.
units.literal: From Tianbao year 5 onward, when one man lost virtue, sustaining and rescue in truth had reliance in him.

units.zh: 每天子臨軒，公卿拜授，施號發令，宣揚詔冊。
units.en: Whenever the emperor appeared at court for investitures and edicts, Yang Yin proclaimed the orders and read out the imperial writs.
units.literal: Whenever the Son of Heaven came to the hall, the lords and ministers received investiture in obeisance; he issued names and sent forth orders, proclaiming edicts and registers.

units.zh: 愔辭氣溫辯，神儀秀發，百僚觀聽，莫不悚動。
units.en: Yang Yin's diction was warm and fluent, his bearing brilliant; the officials who watched and listened were all stirred.
units.literal: Yin's diction was warm and eloquent, his bearing brilliant; the hundred officials watching and listening were all stirred and awed.

units.zh: 自居大位，門絕私交。
units.en: From the time he rose to supreme power he shut his gate to private friendships.
units.literal: From the time he occupied the high seat, his gate cut off private friendship.

units.zh: 輕貨財，重仁義，前後賞賜，積累巨萬，散之九族，架篋之中，唯有書數千卷。
units.en: He valued righteousness over wealth; rewards that accumulated to vast sums he gave away among his clansmen, and in his cupboards he kept only several thousand books.
units.literal: He held goods light and weight righteousness heavy; rewards before and after accumulated in the tens of thousands—he dispersed them among the nine clans; in his shelves and boxes there were only several thousand scrolls of books.

units.zh: 太保、平原王隆之與愔鄰宅，愔嘗見其門外有富胡數人，謂左右曰：「我門前幸無此物。」
units.en: Grand mentor Prince Longzhi of Pingyuan lived next to Yang Yin. Yin once saw several wealthy foreigners at Longzhi's gate and told his attendants, "Fortunately there is none of that at my gate."
units.literal: Grand Mentor, Prince Longzhi of Pingyuan, was Yang Yin's neighbor; Yin once saw several rich Hu men outside his gate and told his attendants, "Fortunately there is no such thing before my gate."

units.zh: 性周密畏慎，恒若不足，每聞後命，愀然變色。
units.en: His nature was thorough and cautious, always as if he fell short; whenever he heard a fresh order his face fell.
units.literal: His nature was thorough, cautious and timid, always as if insufficient; whenever he heard a later command his expression changed mournfully.

units.zh: 文宣大漸，以常山、長廣二王位地親逼，深以後事為念。
units.en: As Emperor Wenxuan sank toward death, he worried deeply about the aftermath, for the princes of Changshan and Changgung stood too close in kinship and power.
units.literal: When Wenxuan was critically ill, because the princes of Changshan and Changgung were close in rank and kin and pressed near, he was deeply concerned about what would follow.

units.zh: 愔與尚書左僕射平秦王歸彥、侍中燕子獻、黃門侍郎鄭子默受遺詔輔政，並以二王威望先重，咸有猜忌之心。
units.en: Yang Yin with left vice director Prince Guiyan of Pingqin, palace attendant Yan Zixian, and yellow gate vice director Zheng Zimo received the deathbed testament to govern as regents; because the two princes already carried such weight, all harbored suspicion.
units.literal: Yin with Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Prince Guiyan of Pingqin, Palace Attendant Yan Zixian, and Yellow Gate Vice Director Zheng Zimo received the testament to assist government; they all, because the two princes' prestige was already heavy, had hearts of suspicion.

units.zh: 初在晉陽，以大行在殯，天子諒暗，議令常山王在東館，欲奏之事，皆先諮決。
units.en: At first in Jinyang, while the late emperor lay in state and the young emperor mourned in seclusion, the regents proposed that the prince of Changshan stay at the eastern lodge and that all memorials pass through him first.
units.literal: At first in Jinyang, because the departed lay in encoffining and the Son of Heaven was in mourning gloom, it was proposed that the prince of Changshan stay at the eastern lodge; whatever one wished to memorialize should first be consulted and decided.

units.zh: 二旬而止。
units.en: This lasted twenty days and then ceased.
units.literal: After twenty days it stopped.

units.zh: 仍欲以常山王隨梓宮之鄴，留長廣王鎮晉陽。
units.en: They next wished the prince of Changshan to accompany the coffin to Ye and the prince of Changgung to hold Jinyang.
units.literal: They still wished the prince of Changshan to follow the coffin to Ye and leave the prince of Changgung to garrison Jinyang.

units.zh: 執政復生疑貳，兩王又俱從至于鄴。
units.en: The regents again grew divided and doubtful, and both princes followed on to Ye together.
units.literal: The ruling ministers again bred doubt and division; both princes again both followed and arrived at Ye.

units.zh: 子獻立計，欲處太皇太后於北宮，政歸皇太后。
units.en: Zixian proposed housing the grand empress dowager in the northern palace so that power would rest with the empress dowager.
units.literal: Zixian set up a plan wishing to place the grand empress dowager in the northern palace and return government to the empress dowager.

units.zh: 又自天保八年已來，爵賞多濫，至是，愔先自表解其開府封王，諸叨竊恩榮者皆從黜免。
units.en: Moreover, since the eighth year of Tianbao enfeoffments and rewards had run wild; now Yin was first to memorial requesting release from his privy chamber and royal title, and all who had improperly gained rank were stripped.
units.literal: Moreover, from Tianbao year 8 titles and rewards had been excessive; at this time Yin first memorialized himself to resign his opening-office enfeoffment as king, and all who had improperly received favor and glory were dismissed.

units.zh: 由是嬖寵失職之徒，盡歸心二叔。
units.en: Hence the displaced favorites all threw their loyalty to the two princes.
units.literal: Hence those of the favorites who lost their posts all turned their hearts to the two uncles.

units.zh: 高歸彥初雖同德，後尋反動，以疏忌之跡盡告兩王。
units.en: Gao Guiyan had first shared their purpose, but soon turned against them and told the two princes everything the regents had done out of suspicion.
units.literal: Gao Guiyan at first thought of the same virtue, later soon turned against them, reporting all traces of estrangement and suspicion to the two princes.

units.zh: 可朱渾天和又每云：「若不誅二王，少主無自安之理。」
units.en: Kezhuhun Tianhe also said repeatedly, "Unless the two princes are killed, the young emperor can never be secure."
units.literal: Kezhuhun Tianhe also often said, "If the two princes are not executed, the young lord has no principle by which to make himself secure."

units.zh: 宋欽道面奏帝，稱二叔威權旣重，宜速去之。
units.en: Song Qindao reported to the emperor in person that the two uncles' power was already too great and they should be removed at once.
units.literal: Song Qindao addressed the emperor in person, saying the two uncles' prestige and power were already heavy and they should quickly be removed.

units.zh: 帝不許曰：「可與令公共詳其事。」
units.en: The emperor refused and said, "Take the matter up in full counsel with the director."
units.literal: The emperor did not consent and said, "This may be jointly examined in detail with the director."

units.zh: 愔等議出二王為刺史。
units.en: Yang Yin and the others debated posting the two princes to provincial inspectorates.
units.literal: Yin and the rest discussed sending the two princes out as inspectors.

units.zh: 以帝仁慈，恐不可所奏，乃通啟皇太后，具述安危。
units.en: Fearing the benevolent emperor would not approve their memorial, they sent a private report to the empress dowager explaining the danger in full.
units.literal: Because the emperor was benevolent, fearing what they memorialized might not be accepted, they sent a sealed report to the empress dowager, setting forth safety and peril in full.

units.zh: 有宮人李昌儀者，北豫州刺史高仲密之妻，坐仲密事入宮，太后以昌儀宗情，甚相昵愛。
units.en: A palace woman named Li Changyi, wife of North Yuzhou inspector Gao Zhongmi, had entered the palace because of her husband's case; the empress dowager, who was kin to Changyi, favored her greatly.
units.literal: There was a palace woman Li Changyi, wife of North Yuzhou Inspector Gao Zhongmi; because of Zhongmi's case she entered the palace; the empress dowager, because of Changyi's clan tie, was very intimate and fond.

units.zh: 太後以啟示之，昌儀密啟太皇太后。
units.en: The empress dowager showed her the report; Changyi secretly informed the grand empress dowager.
units.literal: The empress dowager showed her the report; Changyi secretly reported to the grand empress dowager.

units.zh: 愔等又議不可令二王俱出，乃奏以長廣王為大司馬、幷州刺史，常山王為太師、錄尚書事。
units.en: The regents then decided the two princes must not both leave the capital and memorialized appointing the prince of Changgung grand marshal and Bingzhou inspector, and the prince of Changshan grand preceptor and recorder of the masters of writing.
units.literal: Yin and the rest again discussed that the two princes must not both be sent out; they memorialized making the prince of Changgung Grand Marshal and inspector of Bing, the prince of Changshan Grand Preceptor and recorder of the masters of writing.

units.zh: 及二王拜職，於尚書省大會百僚，愔等並將同赴。
units.en: When the two princes were to take their offices the court planned a great assembly of officials at the Masters of Writing; Yang Yin and the others were all to attend.
units.literal: When the two princes took office, at the Masters of Writing they convened the hundred officials in great assembly; Yin and the rest were all about to go together.

units.zh: 子默止之，云：「事不可量，不可輕脫。」
units.en: Zimo restrained them, saying, "The outcome cannot be foreseen; do not go unprepared."
units.literal: Zimo stopped them, saying, "The matter cannot be measured—one must not lightly strip off caution."

units.zh: 愔云：「吾等至誠體國，豈有常山拜職，有不赴之理，何為忽有此慮？」
units.en: Yang Yin said, "We serve the state in utter loyalty. How could we fail to attend when the prince of Changshan takes office? Why this sudden fear?"
units.literal: Yin said, "We in utmost sincerity embody the state—how could there be principle in not attending when Changshan takes office? Why suddenly this worry?"

units.zh: 長廣旦伏家僮數十人於錄尚書後室，仍與席上勳貴數人相知。
units.en: The prince of Changgung hid dozens of household slaves in the recorder's rear chamber and confided in several honored nobles at the banquet.
units.literal: The prince of Changgung at dawn hid several tens of household slaves in the rear chamber of the recorder of the masters of writing; moreover he made understanding with several meritorious nobles at the seat.

units.zh: 並與諸勳胄約，行酒至愔等，我各勸雙杯，彼必致辭。
units.en: He agreed with the meritorious young nobles: when wine reaches Yang Yin and the others, each of us urges a double cup—they are sure to decline.
units.literal: He also made a pact with the meritorious scions: when wine comes to Yin and the rest, each of us will urge a double cup; they are sure to decline.

units.zh: 我一曰「捉酒」，二曰「捉酒，」三曰「何不捉，」爾輩即捉。
units.en: At my first call, "seize the wine"; my second, "seize the wine"; and my third, "why not seize it?" You seize them at once.
units.literal: At my first call, "seize the wine"; my second, "seize the wine"; and my third, "why not seize it?" You seize them at once.

units.zh: 及宴如之。
units.en: At the banquet all went as planned.
units.literal: When the banquet came it was as planned.

units.zh: 愔大言曰：「諸王構逆，欲殺忠良邪？
units.en: Yang Yin cried out, "You princes plot treason—do you mean to kill loyal men?
units.literal: Yin shouted, "Princes, you plot rebellion—you wish to kill the loyal and good?

units.zh: 尊天子，削諸侯，赤心奉國，未應及此。」
units.en: We honor the emperor, curtail the princes, and give our loyal hearts to the state—we should not come to this!"
units.literal: Honor the Son of Heaven, reduce the feudal lords—we give our red hearts to serve the state; we ought not come to this."

units.zh: 常山王欲緩之，長廣王曰：「不可。」
units.en: The prince of Changshan wished to relent; the prince of Changgung said, "No."
units.literal: The prince of Changshan wished to ease matters; the prince of Changgung said, "It cannot be."

units.zh: 於是愔及天和、欽道皆被拳杖亂毆擊，頭面血流，各十人持之。
units.en: Thereupon Yang Yin, Tianhe, and Qindao were beaten with fists and clubs until blood ran from their heads and faces; ten men held each of them.
units.literal: Thereupon Yin and Tianhe and Qindao were all struck and beaten in disorder with fists and staves; heads and faces streamed blood; ten men each held them.

units.zh: 使薛孤延、康買執子默於尚藥局。
units.en: They sent Xue Guyan and Kang Mai to seize Zimo at the imperial pharmacy bureau.
units.literal: They sent Xue Guyan and Kang Mai to seize Zimo at the Bureau of Imperial Pharmacy.

units.zh: 子默曰：「不用智者言，以至於此，豈非命也！」
units.en: Zimo said, "By not heeding the wise man's counsel we have come to this—is it not fate?"
units.literal: Zimo said, "By not using the wise man's words we have come to this—is it not fate!

units.zh: 二叔率高歸彥、賀拔仁、斛律金擁愔等唐突入雲龍門。
units.en: The two princes led Gao Guiyan, Heba Ren, and Hulu Jin in hustling Yang Yin and the others through Cloud Dragon Gate.
units.literal: The two uncles led Gao Guiyan, Heba Ren, and Hulu Jin in hustling Yin and the rest in a rush through Cloud Dragon Gate.

units.zh: 見都督叱利騷，招之不進，使騎殺之。
units.en: They saw commander Chilü Sao, summoned him, and when he would not advance they had horsemen cut him down.
units.literal: They saw Commander Chilü Sao, summoned him; he would not advance; they had horsemen kill him.

units.zh: 開府成休寧拒門，歸彥喻之，乃得入。
units.en: Cheng Xiuning, who held privy chamber rank, blocked the gate; Guiyan persuaded him, and they entered.
units.literal: Acting Three Excellencies Cheng Xiuning barred the gate; Guiyan instructed him, and only then could they enter.

units.zh: 送愔等於御前。
units.en: They brought Yang Yin and the others before the emperor.
units.literal: They sent Yin and the rest before the emperor.

units.zh: 長廣王及歸彥在朱華門外。
units.en: The prince of Changgung and Guiyan waited outside Vermilion Flower Gate.
units.literal: The prince of Changgung and Guiyan were outside Vermilion Flower Gate.

units.zh: 太皇太后臨昭陽殿，太后及帝側立。
units.en: The grand empress dowager presided in Zhaoyang Hall; the empress dowager and the emperor stood at her side.
units.literal: The grand empress dowager came to Zhaoyang Hall; the empress dowager and the emperor stood at the side.

units.zh: 常山王以磚叩頭，進而言曰：「臣與陛下骨肉相連。
units.en: The prince of Changshan kowtowed on the brick floor and said, "Your servant and Your Majesty are bound in the same flesh.
units.literal: The prince of Changshan knocked his head with brick and advanced, saying, "Your servant and Your Majesty are bone and flesh joined.

units.zh: 楊遵彥等欲擅朝權，威福自己，王公以還，皆重足屏氣。
units.en: Yang Zunyan and his circle meant to monopolize court power and keep bounty in their own hands; from kings and dukes down everyone stood in dread.
units.literal: Yang Zunyan and the rest wished to monopolize court power; authority and blessing were theirs alone; from kings and dukes down all stood on tiptoe and held their breath.

units.zh: 共相唇齒，以成亂階，若不早圖，必為宗社之害。
units.en: They were mouth and gum to one another and piled step on step toward chaos; unless checked early they would ruin the altars of state.
units.literal: They were lip and teeth to each other and made the steps of disorder; if not plotted against early, they would surely harm the altars of state.

units.zh: 臣與湛等為國事重，賀拔仁、斛律金等惜獻皇帝基業，共執遵彥等領入宮，未敢刑戮，專輒之失，罪合萬死。」
units.en: Your servant and Zhan took the weight of state upon ourselves; Heba Ren and Hulu Jin cherished Emperor Xian's foundation; we seized Zunyan and his fellows and brought them into the palace. We have not yet executed them; for our presumption we deserve ten thousand deaths."
units.literal: Your servant and Zhan and the rest took state affairs as weighty; Heba Ren, Hulu Jin and the rest cherished Emperor Xian's foundation; together we seized Zunyan and the rest and led them into the palace; we did not yet dare execution and punishment; the fault of arrogating authority deserves ten thousand deaths."

units.zh: 帝時默然，領軍劉桃枝之徒陛衛，叩刀仰視，帝不睨之，太皇太后令卻仗，不肯。
units.en: The emperor said nothing. Garrison-general Liu Taozhi and his guards stood on the stairs, hands on their blades, looking up at him; the emperor would not meet their eyes. The grand empress dowager ordered them to stand down; they refused.
units.literal: The emperor was silent; Liu Taozhi of the garrison-general and his kind guarded the steps, striking blades and looking up; the emperor would not glance at them; the grand empress dowager ordered them to lay aside weapons; they would not.

units.zh: 又厲聲曰：「奴輩即今頭落。」
units.en: She shouted again, "Slaves—off with your heads this instant!"
units.literal: She again said in a harsh voice, "Slaves—your heads fall this instant."

units.zh: 乃卻。
units.en: Then they withdrew.
units.literal: Then they withdrew.

units.zh: 因問楊郎何在，賀拔仁曰：「一目已出。」
units.en: She asked where Master Yang was; Heba Ren said, "One eye is already gone."
units.literal: She then asked where Master Yang was; Heba Ren said, "One eye is already out."

units.zh: 太皇太后愴然曰：「楊郎何所能，留使不好耶！」
units.en: The grand empress dowager said in grief, "What harm could Master Yang have done—was it not better to keep him!"
units.literal: The grand empress dowager said mournfully, "What could Master Yang do—would it not have been better to keep him!"

units.zh: 乃讓帝曰：「此等懷逆，欲殺我二兒，次及我，爾何縱之？」
units.en: She reproached the emperor: "These men plotted rebellion; they meant to kill my two sons and next would reach me—why did you indulge them?"
units.literal: She then reproached the emperor: "These men harbored rebellion, wished to kill my two sons, next would reach me—why did you indulge them?"

units.zh: 帝猶不能言。
units.en: The emperor still could not speak.
units.literal: The emperor still could not speak.

units.zh: 太皇太后怒且悲，王公皆泣。
units.en: The grand empress dowager was torn between anger and grief; the princes and dukes wept.
units.literal: The grand empress dowager was angry and grieved; kings and dukes all wept.

units.zh: 太皇太后曰：「豈可使我母子受漢老嫗斟酌。」
units.en: The grand empress dowager said, "How can you let us mother and son be ruled by an old Han woman!"
units.literal: The grand empress dowager said, "How can you let us mother and son be measured out by an old Han crone!"

units.zh: 太后拜謝。
units.en: The empress dowager bowed in apology.
units.literal: The empress dowager bowed in apology.

units.zh: 常山王叩頭不止。
units.en: The prince of Changshan kept knocking his head on the floor.
units.literal: The prince of Changshan knocked his head without cease.

units.zh: 太皇太后謂帝：「何不安尉爾叔？」
units.en: The grand empress dowager said to the emperor, "Why do you not comfort your uncle?"
units.literal: The grand empress dowager said to the emperor, "Why do you not comfort and soothe your uncle?"

units.zh: 帝乃曰：「天子亦不敢與叔惜，豈敢惜此漢輩？
units.en: The emperor then said, "Even the Son of Heaven dares not withhold them from his uncle—how much less these Han fellows?
units.literal: The emperor then said, "The Son of Heaven also dares not spare them for his uncle's sake—how much less spare these Han fellows?

units.zh: 但願乞兒性命，兒自下殿去，此等任叔父處分。」
units.en: I beg only for my son's life; your son will leave the hall—dispose of this lot as you will."
units.literal: I only wish to beg my son's life; your son will leave the hall—this lot is left to uncle's disposal."

units.zh: 遂皆斬之。
units.en: Thereupon all were beheaded.
units.literal: Thereupon all were beheaded.

units.zh: 長廣王以子默昔讒己作詔書，故先拔其舌，截其手。
units.en: The prince of Changgung, because Zimo had once slandered him in an edict, first tore out his tongue and cut off his hands.
units.literal: The prince of Changgung, because Zimo had once slandered him in drafting an edict, first pulled out his tongue and cut off his hands.

units.zh: 太皇太后臨愔喪，哭曰：「楊郎忠而獲罪。」
units.en: The grand empress dowager attended Yang Yin's mourning and wept, "Master Yang was loyal yet was punished."
units.literal: The grand empress dowager attended Yin's mourning and wept, saying, "Master Yang was loyal yet received punishment."

units.zh: 以御金為之一眼，親內之，曰：「以表我意。」
units.en: She had an eye made of imperial gold and placed it in the coffin herself, saying, "This shows my heart."
units.literal: She used imperial gold to make one eye, personally placed it within, and said, "To show my mind."

units.zh: 常山王亦悔殺之。
units.en: The prince of Changshan also regretted the killing.
units.literal: The prince of Changshan also regretted killing him.

units.zh: 先是童謠曰：「白羊頭尾禿，羖䍽頭生角。」
units.en: Earlier a children's rhyme ran, "The white sheep's head and tail are bare; the black ram grows horns on its brow."
units.literal: Before this, a children's rhyme said, "The white sheep's head and tail are bald; the black ram's head grows horns."

units.zh: 又曰：「羊羊喫野草，不吃野草遠我道，不遠打爾腦。」
units.en: Another ran, "Sheep, sheep, graze the wild grass; leave the grass and you leave my road; stay near and I'll crack your skull."
units.literal: It also said, "Sheep, sheep eat wild grass; if you don't eat wild grass, keep far from my road; if you don't keep far, I'll beat your brains."

units.zh: 又曰：「阿麼姑禍也，道人姑夫死也。」
units.en: Another said, "Auntie brings ruin; the tonsured princess's husbands die."
units.literal: It also said, "Auntie brings calamity; the Daoist nun's brother-in-law dies."

units.zh: 羊為愔也，「角」文為用刀，「道人」謂廢帝小名，太原公主嘗作尼，故曰「阿麼姑」，愔子獻、天和皆帝姑夫云。
units.en: Sheep stood for Yin; the character for 'horn' splits into 'use' and 'knife'; 'Daoist' meant the deposed emperor's childhood name; the princess of Taiyuan had once been a nun, hence 'Auntie'; Zixian and Tianhe, both sons-in-law of the house, were tied to the rhyme.
units.literal: Sheep was Yin; 'horn' written was using a knife; 'Daoist' meant the deposed emperor's childhood name; the princess of Taiyuan had once been a nun, hence 'Auntie'; Yin, Zixian, and Tianhe were all the emperor's aunts' husbands.

units.zh: 於是乃以天子之命下詔罪之，罪止一身，家口不問。
units.en: Thereupon an edict in the emperor's name condemned them, limiting guilt to the men themselves and exempting their households.
units.literal: Thereupon by the Son of Heaven's command an edict was issued condemning their crimes; guilt stopped at one person; households were not questioned.

units.zh: 尋復簿錄五家，王晞固諫，乃各沒一房，孩幼兄弟皆除名。
units.en: Before long registers were drawn up against five families; Wang Xi protested firmly; in the end one branch of each house was confiscated and brothers and children were struck from the rolls.
units.literal: Soon registers were again made of five families; Wang Xi firmly remonstrated; thereupon one branch of each was confiscated; infant children and brothers were all struck from the rolls.

units.zh: 遵彥死，仍以中書令趙彥深代總機務。
units.en: After Zunyan's death, secretariat director Zhao Yanshen was put in charge of state affairs in his place.
units.literal: When Zunyan died, Secretariat Director Zhao Yanshen was still used to replace him in overseeing critical affairs.

units.zh: 鴻臚少卿陽休之私謂人曰：「將涉千里，殺騏驥而策蹇驢，可悲之甚。」
units.en: Palace reception vice director Yang Xiuzhi said privately, "One is about to cross a thousand li, yet kills the qilin and drives a lame donkey—how pitiful."
units.literal: Palace Reception Vice Director Yang Xiuzhi said privately to someone, "About to cross a thousand li, yet killing the qilin and driving the lame donkey—how deeply pitiable."

units.zh: 愔所著詩賦表奏書訟甚多，誅後散失，門生鳩集所得者萬餘言。
units.en: Yang Yin left many poems, fu, memorials, and pleading documents; after his execution most were lost, but his disciples gathered more than ten thousand words of what survived.
units.literal: Yin's compositions in poetry, rhapsodies, memorials, and legal briefs were very many; after execution they were scattered and lost; what his disciples gathered amounted to more than ten thousand words.

units.zh: 燕子獻，字季則，廣漢下洛人。
units.en: Yan Zixian, styled Jize, was from Xialuo in Guanghan.
units.literal: Yan Zixian, styled Jize, was from Xialuo in Guanghan.

units.zh: 少時相者謂之曰：「使役在胡代，富貴在齊趙。」
units.en: When he was young, a physiognomist told him, "Your service will be among Hu and Dai, and your wealth and rank in Qi and Zhao."
units.literal: When he was young, a physiognomist said to him, "Your service will be among Hu and Dai, and your wealth and rank in Qi and Zhao."

units.zh: 其後，遇宇文氏稱霸關中，用為典簽，將命使於茹茹。
units.en: Later, when the Yuwen clan rose to hegemony in Guanzhong, he was employed as a records clerk and sent on a mission to Rouran.
units.literal: Later, when the Yuwen clan claimed hegemony in Guanzhong, he was employed as a records clerk and was sent on a mission to Rouran.

units.zh: 子獻欲驗相者之言，來歸。
units.en: Zixian wanted to test the physiognomist's prediction, so he came over in submission.
units.literal: Zixian wished to test the physiognomist's words and came over in submission.

units.zh: 高祖見之大悅，尚淮陽公主，甚被待遇。
units.en: Gaozu was delighted when he met him; Zixian married Princess Huaiyang and received especially favorable treatment.
units.literal: Gaozu saw him and was greatly pleased; he married Princess Huaiyang and was treated very favorably.

units.zh: 顯祖時，官至侍中、開府。
units.en: In Xianzu's time, he rose to palace attendant and opening office.
units.literal: In Xianzu's time, his offices reached palace attendant and opening office.

units.zh: 濟南即位之後，委任彌重，除右僕射。
units.en: After Jinan ascended the throne, he was entrusted with even greater responsibility and appointed right vice director.
units.literal: After Jinan ascended the throne, his entrusted responsibilities became still weightier, and he was appointed right vice director.

units.zh: 子獻素多力，頭又少發，當狼狽之際，排衆走出省門，斛律光逐而擒之。
units.en: Zixian was always strong and had little hair. In the panic he pushed through the crowd and fled out the office gate, but Hulu Guang pursued and seized him.
units.literal: Zixian had always been strong and had little hair on his head; in the moment of panic he pushed through the crowd and fled out the office gate, but Hulu Guang pursued and seized him.

units.zh: 子獻嘆曰：「丈夫為計遲，遂至於此矣。」
units.en: Zixian sighed, "A man planned too late, and so it has come to this."
units.literal: Zixian sighed and said, "A man made his plan too late and so has come to this."

units.zh: 可朱渾天和，道元之季弟也。
units.en: Kezhuhun Tianhe was the youngest brother of Daoyuan.
units.literal: Kezhuhun Tianhe was Daoyuan's youngest brother.

units.zh: 以道無勳重，尚東平公主。
units.en: Because his clan had little merit he was married to the princess of Dongping.
units.literal: Because Daoyuan had no weight of merit, he married the princess of Dongping.

units.zh: 累遷領軍大將軍、開府。
units.en: He rose through posts to garrison-general, grand general, and privy chamber.
units.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to garrison-general grand general and privy chamber.

units.zh: 濟南王即位，加特進，改博陵公，與楊愔同被殺。
units.en: When the prince of Jinan took the throne he was made special advance and duke of Boling, and was killed together with Yang Yin.
units.literal: When the prince of Jinan took the throne he was given special advance, changed to Duke of Boling, and was killed together with Yang Yin.

units.zh: 宋欽道，廣平人，魏吏部尚書弁孫也。
units.en: Song Qindao was from Guangping, grandson of Wei minister of personnel Song Bian.
units.literal: Song Qindao was a man of Guangping, grandson of Wei Minister of Personnel Bian.

units.zh: 初為大將軍主簿，典書記。
units.en: He began as chief clerk to the grand general, keeping the records.
units.literal: At first he was chief clerk to the grand general, in charge of records.

units.zh: 後為黃門侍郎。
units.en: Later he became yellow gate vice director.
units.literal: Later he was yellow gate vice director.

units.zh: 又令在東宮教太子習事。
units.en: He was also assigned to the eastern palace to instruct the crown prince in affairs of state.
units.literal: He was also ordered to the eastern palace to teach the heir apparent administrative matters.

units.zh: 時鄭子默以文學見知，亦備親寵。
units.en: At that time Zheng Zimo was known for his learning and shared intimate favor at court.
units.literal: At the time Zheng Zimo was known for literary accomplishment and also enjoyed intimate favor.

units.zh: 欽道本文法吏，不甚諳識古今，凡有疑事，必詢於子默。
units.en: Qindao was by training a legal clerk, not deeply versed in history; whenever he was unsure he asked Zimo.
units.literal: Qindao by origin was a clerk versed in statutes, not very familiar with past and present; whenever there was a doubtful matter he always inquired of Zimo.

units.zh: 二人幸於兩宮，雖諸王貴臣莫不敬憚。
units.en: Both were favorites of the two palaces; even princes and great ministers feared them.
units.literal: The two men were favored by both palaces; even princes and eminent ministers did not fail to respect and fear them.

units.zh: 欽道又遷秘書監。
units.en: Qindao was later promoted to director of the secretariat library.
units.literal: Qindao was again promoted to director of the secretariat library.

units.zh: 與楊愔同誅，贈吏部尚書、趙州刺史。
units.en: He was executed with Yang Yin and posthumously made minister of personnel and inspector of Zhao.
units.literal: He was executed together with Yang Yin; posthumously granted Minister of Personnel and inspector of Zhao.

units.zh: 鄭頤，字子默，彭城人。
units.en: Zheng Yi, style Zimo, was a man of Pengcheng.
units.literal: Zheng Yi, style Zimo, was a man of Pengcheng.

units.zh: 高祖據，魏彭城守，自滎陽徙焉。
units.en: His distant ancestor Ju held Pengcheng for Wei and moved there from Xingyang.
units.literal: High ancestor Ju held Pengcheng for Wei and moved from Xingyang thither.

units.zh: 頤聰敏，頗涉文義。
units.en: Yi was clever and well read in the literary tradition.
units.literal: Yi was clever and quick, and had broadly touched literary meaning.

units.zh: 初為太原公東閣祭酒，與宋欽道特相友愛，欽道每師事之。
units.en: He first served as eastern-pavilion libationer to the prince of Taiyuan and was especially close to Song Qindao, who treated him as his teacher.
units.literal: At first he was eastern-pavilion libationer to the prince of Taiyuan, and was especially friendly with Song Qindao; Qindao always treated him as master.

units.zh: 楊愔始輕宋、鄭，不為之禮。
units.en: Yang Yin at first despised Song and Zheng and did not treat them with courtesy.
units.literal: Yang Yin at first looked down on Song and Zheng and did not extend ceremony to them.

units.zh: 俄而自結人主，與參顧命。
units.en: Before long Zheng Yi bound himself to the ruler and joined the regency.
units.literal: Before long he bound himself to the ruler and participated in the deathbed testament.

units.zh: 欽道復舊與濟南款狎，共相引致，無所不言。
units.en: Qindao renewed his old closeness with the prince of Jinan; they drew each other on and held nothing back.
units.literal: Qindao renewed his old intimacy with Jinan and mutual introduction; nothing was left unsaid.

units.zh: 乾明初，拜散騎常侍。
units.en: At the beginning of Qianming Zheng Yi was made attendant cavalier in regular attendance.
units.literal: At the beginning of Qianming he was appointed attendant cavalier in regular attendance.

units.zh: 二人權勢之重，與愔相埒。
units.en: The two men's authority weighed as heavily as Yin's.
units.literal: The two men's weight of power was on a par with Yin.

units.zh: 愔見害之時，邢子才流涕曰：「楊令君雖其人，死日恨不得一佳伴。」
units.en: When Yin was killed, Xing Zicai wept and said, "Lord Yang was truly such a man — on the day of his death, how one wished he had a worthy companion at his side."
units.literal: When Yin met his death, Xing Zicai wept and said: "Magistrate Yang was indeed such a man; at the day of death one regrets he could not have one worthy companion."

units.zh: 頤後與愔同詔追贈殿中尚書、廣州刺史。
units.en: Later, by the same edict as Yin, Yi was posthumously made palace secretary and inspector of Guangzhou.
units.literal: Later Yi was by the same edict as Yin posthumously granted Director within the Palace and Inspector of Guangzhou.

units.zh: 頤弟抗，字子信，頗有文學。
units.en: Yi's younger brother Kang, styled Zixin, was well versed in letters.
units.literal: Yi's younger brother Kang, style Zixin, had considerable accomplishment in letters.

units.zh: 武平末，兼左右郎中，待詔文林館。
units.en: At the end of Wuping he served concurrently as left and right langzhong, awaiting summons at the Forest of Literary Excellence.
units.literal: At the end of Wuping, he concurrently served as Left and Right Langzhong, awaiting summons at the Forest of Literary Excellence.

units.zh: 論曰：愔雅道風流，早同標緻，公望人物所推。
units.en: The appraisal says: Yang Yin's elegant conduct and refined style marked him early as a model, and he was highly regarded in both public reputation and personal quality.
units.literal: The appraisal says: Yin's elegant way and refined style early matched a distinguished standard, and in public reputation and personal quality he was highly regarded.

units.zh: 夫處亂虐之世，當機衡之重，朝有善政，是也。
units.en: To live in an age of disorder and cruelty, bear the weight of government, and still bring good policies to court was a real achievement.
units.literal: To dwell in an age of disorder and cruelty, bear the weight of the pivot of government, and have good policies at court: this was right.

units.zh: 及寄天下之命，托六尺之孤，旬朔未幾，身亡君辱。
units.en: But when the fate of the realm was entrusted to him and the young orphan ruler placed in his care, before even ten days or a month had passed, he was dead and his ruler humiliated.
units.literal: But when the fate of the realm was entrusted to him and a six-chi orphan was placed in his care, before even ten days or a month had passed, his body was destroyed and his ruler humiliated.

units.zh: 進不能送往事居，觀幾衛主；
units.en: Advancing, he could not send off the dead, serve the living, read the signs, and protect his ruler;
units.literal: Advancing, he could not send off the dead and serve the living, observe the signs, and protect his ruler;

units.zh: 退不能保身全名，辭寵招福。
units.en: retreating, he could not preserve himself and his name, decline favor, and invite good fortune.
units.literal: retreating, he could not preserve his body and keep his name whole, decline favor, and summon good fortune.

units.zh: 朝廷之釁，既已仗義斷恩；
units.en: The rupture at court had already forced him to stand on righteousness and sever personal ties;
units.literal: The rupture at court had already made him rely on righteousness and cut off personal affection;

units.zh: 猜忌之塗，無容推心受亂。
units.en: on the path of suspicion and jealousy, there was no room to open his heart and accept disorder.
units.literal: on the path of suspicion and jealousy, there was no room to open his heart and accept disorder.

units.zh: 是知變通之術，非所長也。
units.en: Thus we know that the art of adaptation was not his strength.
units.literal: From this we know that the art of adaptation was not what he was good at.

units.zh: 二月己亥，以太傅、常山王演爲太師、錄尚書事，以太尉、長廣王湛爲大司馬、幷省錄尚書事，以尚書左僕射、平秦王歸彥爲司空，趙郡王叡爲尚書左僕射。
units.en: In the second month, on jihai, Prince Yan of Changshan, then grand tutor, was appointed grand preceptor and recorder of the Masters of Writing. Prince Zhan of Changguang, then grand commandant, became grand marshal and recorder of the Masters of Writing in the Bingzhou administration. Prince Guiyan of Pingqin, left vice director of the Masters of Writing, became minister of works, and Prince Rui of Zhaojun became left vice director.
units.literal: In the second month, on jihai, the Grand Tutor, Prince Yan of Changshan, was made Grand Preceptor and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing; the Grand Commandant, Prince Zhan of Changguang, was made Grand Marshal and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing in Bing Province; the Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Prince Guiyan of Pingqin, was made Minister of Works; and Prince Rui of Zhaojun was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

units.zh: 皇建二年秋，天文告變，歸彥慮有後害，仍白孝昭，以王當咎。
units.en: In autumn of Huangjian 2, ominous celestial signs appeared. Guiyan feared future trouble and again told Emperor Xiaozhao that the prince was the one portended by the omen.
units.literal: In autumn of the second year of Huangjian, celestial signs announced change; Guiyan feared there would be later danger, and again told Xiaozhao that the prince was the one on whom blame would fall.

units.zh: 乃遣歸彥馳驛至晉陽宮殺之。
units.en: He therefore sent Guiyan by relay post to Jinyang Palace to kill him.
units.literal: He therefore sent Guiyan by relay horse to Jinyang Palace to kill him.

units.zh: 戊申，以常山王演爲大丞相、都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事，以大司馬、長廣王湛爲太傅、京畿大都督，以司徒段韶爲大將軍，以前司空、平陽王淹爲太尉，以司空、平秦王歸彥爲司徒，彭城王浟爲尚書令。
units.en: On the wushen day, Prince Yan of Changshan was appointed grand chief minister, commander of all armies, and recorder of the Masters of Writing. Prince Zhan of Changguang, grand marshal, became grand tutor and metropolitan commander of the capital region. Duan Shao, minister over the masses, became great general; Prince Yan of Pingyang, formerly minister of works, became grand commandant; Prince Guiyan of Pingqin, minister of works, became minister over the masses; and Prince You of Pengcheng became director of the Masters of Writing.
units.literal: On the wushen day, Prince Yan of Changshan was made grand chief minister, commander-in-chief of all armies at home and abroad, and recorder of the affairs of the Masters of Writing; Prince Zhan of Changguang, grand marshal, was made grand tutor and metropolitan commander of the capital region; Duan Shao, minister over the masses, was made great general; the former minister of works, Prince Yan of Pingyang, was made grand commandant; Prince Guiyan of Pingqin, minister of works, was made minister over the masses; and Prince You of Pengcheng was made director of the Masters of Writing.

units.zh: 常山王憂悵，乃白太后誅其黨，時平秦王歸彥亦預謀焉。
units.en: Prince Yan of Changshan grew anxious and asked the empress dowager to execute that faction; Prince Guiyan of Pingqin was also involved in the plot.
units.literal: The Prince of Changshan became anxious and distressed, and so reported to the empress dowager that their party should be executed; at the time Prince Guiyan of Pingqin also took part in the plot.

units.zh: 孝昭皇帝演，字延安，神武皇帝第六子，文宣皇帝之母弟也。
units.en: Emperor Xiaozhao, whose personal name was Yan and style name Yan'an, was the sixth son of Emperor Shenwu and the full younger brother of Emperor Wenxuan.
units.literal: Emperor Xiaozhao Yan, styled Yan'an, was the sixth son of Emperor Shenwu and the younger brother of Emperor Wenxuan by the same mother.

units.zh: 大寧元年閏十二月癸卯，梓宮還鄴，上諡曰孝昭皇帝。
units.en: In the intercalary twelfth month of Daning 1, on guimao, his coffin was returned to Ye, and he was given the posthumous title Emperor Xiaozhao.
units.literal: In the intercalary twelfth month of the first year of Daning, on guimao, the imperial coffin returned to Ye, and the posthumous title Emperor Xiaozhao was presented.

units.zh: 魏元象元年，封常山郡公。
units.en: In the first year of the Yuanxiang era of Wei, he was made Duke of Changshan Commandery.
units.literal: In the first year of Yuanxiang of Wei, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Changshan Commandery.

units.zh: 唯常山王至，內外肅然。
units.en: Only when the Prince of Changshan appeared did the palace fall silent and straighten itself.
units.literal: Only when the Prince of Changshan arrived would inside and outside become solemn and awestruck.

units.zh: 皇建元年八月壬午，皇帝即位於晉陽宣德殿，大赦，改乾明元年為皇建。
units.en: On the renwu day of the eighth month of the first year of Huangjian, the emperor ascended the throne in the Xuande Hall at Jinyang, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name from Qianming to Huangjian.
units.literal: On the renwu day of the eighth month of Huangjian year 1, the emperor ascended the throne in the Xuande Hall at Jinyang, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name from Qianming year 1 to Huangjian.

units.zh: 五年，除幷省尚書令。
units.en: In the fifth year he was made Chief Minister of the Secretariat for the combined provinces.
units.literal: In the fifth year, he was appointed Chief Minister of the Secretariat of the Joint Provinces.

units.zh: 八年，轉司空、錄尚書事。
units.en: In the eighth year he was made Minister of Works and Recorder of the Affairs of the Secretariat.
units.literal: In the eighth year, he was transferred to Minister of Works and made Recorder of the Affairs of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 帝長於政術，剖斷咸盡其理，文宣歎重之。
units.en: The prince had a gift for statecraft; every ruling he handed down went to the heart of the matter, and Emperor Wenxuan marveled at him.
units.literal: The Emperor excelled in the art of governance; his analyses and judgments all exhaustively addressed the principles involved, and Wenxuan sighed in admiration and held him in high esteem.

units.zh: 幼而英特，早有大成之量，武明皇太后早所愛重。
units.en: Even as a boy he was remarkable, showing early promise of greatness, and Empress Dowager Wuming had cherished him from the start.
units.literal: From childhood he was outstanding; early on he showed the measure of great accomplishment, and Empress Dowager Wuming had loved and esteemed him from the first.

units.zh: 及文襄執政，遣中書侍郎李同軌就霸府為諸弟師。
units.en: Once Wenxiang took charge of the government, he dispatched Li Tonggui, Gentleman of the Secretariat, to the Overlord's residence to instruct his younger brothers.
units.literal: When Wenxiang came to hold power, he sent Secretariat Gentleman Li Tonggui to the Overlord's residence to serve as tutor to the younger brothers.

units.zh: 右丞相、長廣王湛研機測化，體道居宗，人雄之望，海內瞻仰，同胞共氣，家國所憑，可遣尚書左僕射、趙郡王叡喻旨，征王統茲大寶。
units.en: Prince Zhan of Changguang, right chancellor, understands hidden workings and change, embodies the Way, and stands foremost among the clan. The whole realm looks to him as a hero among men. Born of the same mother and sharing the same breath, he is the support of house and state. Send Prince Rui of Zhaojun, left vice director of the Masters of Writing, to convey my intent and summon him to take charge of the throne.
units.literal: The Right Chancellor, Prince Zhan of Changguang, studies subtle workings and fathoms transformation, embodies the Way and stands within the clan; as a hero among men, he is looked up to within the seas. Of the same womb and shared breath, he is one on whom house and state rely. The Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Prince Rui of Zhaojun, may be sent to explain the intent and summon the prince to govern this great treasure.

units.zh: 順成后本魏朝宗室，文宣欲帝離之，陰為帝廣求淑媛，望移其寵。
units.en: Empress Shuncheng came from the Wei imperial clan. Emperor Wenxuan wanted the prince to turn from her and secretly searched out worthy beauties for him, hoping to draw his heart elsewhere.
units.literal: Empress Shuncheng was originally of the imperial clan of Wei; Wenxuan wanted the Emperor to distance himself from her, and secretly sought fine ladies widely for the Emperor, hoping to shift his favor.

units.zh: 冬十一月辛亥，立妃元氏為皇后，世子百年為皇太子。
units.en: On the xinhai day of the eleventh month, Consort Yuan was installed as empress and the heir apparent Gao Bainian as crown prince.
units.literal: In the eleventh month of winter, on the xinhai day, Consort Yuan was installed as empress and the heir apparent Bainian as crown prince.

units.zh: 豈幽顯之間，實有報復，將齊之基宇止在於斯，帝欲大之，天不許也？
units.en: Was there retribution at work between the seen and unseen worlds—and was the Northern Qi destined to rise no higher? He sought to expand its domain, but Heaven would not allow it.
units.literal: Was it that between the hidden and the manifest there is truly retribution, and that the foundation of Qi would extend no further—he wished to enlarge it, but Heaven would not permit it?

units.zh: 天保初，進爵為王。
units.en: At the opening of the Tianbao era, he was raised to princely rank.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, his rank was advanced to prince.

units.zh: 九年，除大司馬，仍錄尚書。
units.en: In the ninth year he was made Grand Marshal while retaining his post as Recorder of the Secretariat.
units.literal: In the ninth year, he was appointed Grand Marshal, while still serving as Recorder of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 及文宣崩，帝居禁中護喪事，幼主即位，乃即朝班。
units.en: When Emperor Wenxuan died, Xiaozhao remained in the palace to oversee the funeral. Once the young ruler took the throne, he entered the court ranks.
units.literal: When Wenxuan died, the emperor remained inside the palace to oversee the funeral arrangements; after the young ruler ascended the throne, he then took his place in the court ranks.

units.zh: 除太傅、錄尚書，朝政皆決於帝。
units.en: He was appointed grand tutor and recorder of the Masters of Writing, and all court affairs were decided by him.
units.literal: He was appointed Grand Tutor and Recorder of the Masters of Writing, and all court government was decided by the emperor.

units.zh: 時楊愔、燕子獻、可朱渾天和、宋欽道、鄭子默等以帝威望旣重，內懼權逼，請以帝為太師、司州牧、錄尚書事；
units.en: At the time Yang Yin, Yanzi Xian, Kezhuhun Tianhe, Song Qindao, Zheng Zimo, and the others saw how great his prestige had become and secretly feared the pressure of his authority. They asked that he be made grand preceptor, governor of Sizhou, and recorder of the Masters of Writing;
units.literal: At the time Yang Yin, Yanzi Xian, Kezhuhun Tianhe, Song Qindao, Zheng Zimo, and others, because the emperor’s prestige had become weighty and they inwardly feared the pressure of his power, requested that he be made Grand Preceptor, governor of Sizhou, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing;

units.zh: 詔以帝為大丞相、都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事，相府佐史進位一等。
units.en: An edict appointed him Grand Chancellor, Commander-in-Chief of all armies at home and abroad, and Recorder of the Affairs of the Secretariat, and all staff of the chancellery were promoted one rank.
units.literal: An edict appointed the Emperor Grand Chancellor, Commander-in-Chief of all armies at home and abroad, and Recorder of the Affairs of the Secretariat; assistants and clerks of the chancellery were promoted one rank.

units.zh: 先是帝不豫而無闕聽覽，是月，崩於晉陽宮，時年二十七。
units.en: Before this the emperor had been ill, yet he had not neglected audiences or reviews of affairs. That month he died in Jinyang Palace at the age of twenty-seven.
units.literal: Before this, the emperor had been ill but had not neglected hearings and review; that month he died in Jinyang Palace, aged twenty-seven.

units.zh: 庚午，葬於文靖陵。
units.en: On gengwu he was buried in Wenjing Mausoleum.
units.literal: On gengwu, he was buried in Wenjing Mausoleum.

units.zh: 身長八尺，腰帶十圍，儀望風表，迥然獨秀。
units.en: He stood eight feet tall, with a waist ten spans around; in bearing and presence he stood apart, towering above all others.
units.literal: He stood eight feet tall, with a waist ten spans around; in bearing and appearance he stood alone, towering above others.

units.zh: 帝聰敏有識度，深沉能斷，不可窺測。
units.en: The emperor was quick-witted and far-sighted, deep and decisive—his inner thoughts could not be read.
units.literal: The emperor was keen and perceptive, with breadth of judgment; deep and resolute, he could not be fathomed.

units.zh: 澤率爾對曰：「陛下聰明至公，自可遠侔古昔，而有識之士，咸言傷細，帝王之度，頗為未弘。」
units.en: Pei Ze answered without hesitation: "Your Majesty is intelligent and utterly fair and could indeed rival the sages of antiquity, but men of discernment all say you are too exacting in small matters—the magnanimity proper to an emperor is still somewhat lacking."
units.literal: Ze answered straight off: "Your Majesty is intelligent and utterly fair and could indeed rival the ancients of old, but men of discernment all say you are too exacting in small matters; the magnanimity proper to an emperor is still somewhat lacking."

units.zh: 帝又密撰事條，將諫，其友王晞以為不可。
units.en: The prince secretly drew up a list of grievances and prepared to remonstrate, but his friend Wang Xi urged him not to.
